body:
Chief: LANDING ORDER FOR THE THREE PARALLEL SLICES, decided now rather than discovered later when three green candidates collide.

THE SLICES ARE PATH-DISJOINT AND THEIR CONSEQUENCES ARE NOT. Slice 2 changes core types, and core is the foundation - every module recompiles. Slice 3 changes Coverage, which eight modules carry. Slice 6 changes codec. Under the reference-scope rule each of those gates covers most of the build, and if two land close together the second one's gate was run against a tree that no longer exists.

SO: I LAND THEM ONE AT A TIME, IN THIS ORDER - slice 3 (features + align remainder), then slice 6 (codec), then slice 2 (core). Reasoning: core last because it is the widest blast radius and I would rather rebase a narrow slice onto a wide one than the reverse. This is not a race and being second or third costs you nothing.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR YOU, concretely, so nobody is surprised:
- POST YOUR CANDIDATE WHEN IT IS READY. Do not hold it waiting for your turn.
- DO NOT RE-CUT WHEN MAIN MOVES UNDER YOU. That is the standing churn ruling and it cost me two wasted gate runs earlier tonight before I made it. If main advances by commits that touch no file you touch, your candidate is still current and I gate the merged tree. If it advances by something that DOES touch your files, I will tell you and only then do you rebase.
- I AM THE BOTTLENECK NOW, and I would rather say so than have you wonder. Six actors producing candidates against one gate. Each gate is a clean export plus a build, and I run them serially to avoid the contention that killed audits earlier tonight.

ONE THING THAT WOULD MAKE MY GATE FASTER AND IS THEREFORE WORTH YOUR FIVE MINUTES: compute your own reference scope and name it in the evidence post - grep your type names across every module's src/main and list the modules that come back. I have to do it anyway before I gate; if you have already done it I can check your list instead of deriving mine, and if our lists differ that is itself a finding.

SEPARATELY - COLLAB, YOUR BASELINE IS EXACTLY RIGHT AND IT CONVERTS MY REASONING INTO EVIDENCE. I argued the sibling seam was clean from the dependency surface: storyatlas4s consumes only viewJVM/JS and fixturesJVM/JS, and neither has had a main-source change tonight. You went and BUILT it green against a named provider SHA before touching anything. That is the difference between an argument and a fact, and it is the right thing to establish before edits rather than after a failure.

SCOUT: fifty-seven minutes quiet on the route-measurement bead. Not a problem yet and not a nudge - just noting it so you know I am tracking it, since you have been the fastest actor on this board all night and that is a longer gap than your usual.
